title: Analysis and characterization of the carbohydrate fraction of Aiptasia and coral tissue using targeted GC-MS
author: Hagen Gegner

steps.title: Rinse and snap‑freeze samples
steps.instruction: Rinse anemones or coral fragments with double‑distilled water (ddH₂O) to reduce salt load, then transfer anemones to cryotubes or coral fragments to a Falcon tube (or wrap in aluminum foil) and snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Store or continue
steps.instruction: Store the frozen samples at –80 °C, or proceed directly to the next steps if you will continue the protocol immediately.

steps.title: Choose normalization method
steps.instruction: Decide whether to normalise data to total protein content or to dry‑weight. Follow the corresponding branch of the protocol after the initial extraction steps.

steps.title: Add water and transfer to tube
steps.instruction: For Aiptasia add 3 mL ddH₂O and transfer to a Falcon tube. For coral fragments either (a) use an airbrush to remove tissue and add up to 15 mL ddH₂O, or (b) grind frozen tissue with a mortar and pestle cooled in liquid nitrogen, then add up to 15 mL ddH₂O. Transfer the resulting suspension to the appropriate tube.

steps.title: Optional host‑symbiont separation
steps.instruction: If you wish to analyse host and symbiont fractions separately, homogenise the suspension and centrifuge to recover Symbiodinium cells (homogenisation does not destroy the cells).

steps.title: Thaw and add additional water
steps.instruction: Thaw the samples on ice. Add 1 mL ddH₂O to Aiptasia samples. For corals, use an airbrush or crush/pulverise fragments in liquid nitrogen and add up to 15 mL ddH₂O (more water increases downstream processing time).

steps.title: Sonicate homogenate
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice and sonicate with a tip ultrasonicator (e.g., Branson digital sonifier) at 7 W for 2 min until the material is fully dissolved; the homogenate should appear greenish if symbiont cells are cracked open.

steps.title: Remove debris by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 4 000 g for 20 min at 4 °C, keeping the tubes on ice. Discard the pellet and keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation of nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a 50 mL Beckman tube and add cold absolute ethanol in a 9 : 1 ratio (9 parts ethanol to 1 part sample). Mix gently.

steps.title: Incubate precipitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 20 min at 4 °C (or on ice) to precipitate DNA, RNA and protein. While incubating, balance the Beckman tubes for the ultracentrifuge (±0.05 mg).

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 20 000 g for 20 min at 4 °C in a Beckman ultracentrifuge.

steps.title: Recover pellet for protein assay
steps.instruction: Resuspend the resulting pellet in ddH₂O and freeze it for later total‑protein quantification using a BCA protein assay kit (protein‑normalisation branch).

steps.title: Collect supernatant for carbohydrate analysis
steps.instruction: Transfer the cleared supernatant to a new Falcon tube (or pre‑weighed Falcon tube if normalising to dry‑weight).

steps.title: Prepare tubes for lyophilisation
steps.instruction: Place a Kim‑wipe piece on each tube lid, make several small holes in the lid, optionally seal with parafilm, and cool the tubes to –80 °C before loading into the lyophiliser.

steps.title: Lyophilise samples
steps.instruction: Lyophilise the tubes for a minimum of 24 h (overnight) using a freeze‑dryer (e.g., Ultradry).

steps.title: Weigh dried material (dry‑weight branch)
steps.instruction: After lyophilisation, weigh the Falcon tube together with the dried sample; record the weight for later normalisation to dry‑weight.

steps.title: Resuspend dried sample
steps.instruction: Suspend each dried sample in 500 µL ddH₂O (vials can hold up to 2 mL) and vortex vigorously.

steps.title: Transfer to GC vial
steps.instruction: Transfer the suspension to a pre‑labelled GC‑MS vial.

steps.title: Add internal standard
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the internal ISTD to each vial (including calibration standards).

steps.title: Dry sample
steps.instruction: Dry the contents of the vial using a concentrator system (e.g., Labconco Centrivap Complete).

steps.title: Store dried samples
steps.instruction: Keep the dried samples sealed, lid on, and store them in a vacuum desiccator until derivatisation.

steps.title: Add methoxyamine (MOX)
steps.instruction: Using a Hamilton syringe, add 50 µL of MOX reagent to each dried sample, close the vial tightly, and keep the reaction completely free of water (water quenches MOX). Clean the syringe with hexane or cyclohexane before use.

steps.title: Add MSTFA
steps.instruction: Remove the vials from the thermo‑block, add 100 µL of MSTFA with a Hamilton syringe, and use a second syringe to break any clumps so the reagent contacts all material.

steps.title: Incubate derivatisation
steps.instruction: Close the lids tightly and incubate the vials for 1 h at 75 °C in a thermo‑block.

steps.title: Filter derivatised sample
steps.instruction: Pass each reaction through a 0.2 µm (13 mm diameter) syringe filter; transfer 120 µL of the filtrate into a glass insert placed inside a GC vial.

steps.title: Seal and store vials
steps.instruction: Seal the vials with PTFE septa screw caps or crimp caps (crimp caps preferred) and store at –80 °C until GC‑MS measurement.

steps.title: Prepare for GC‑MS measurement
steps.instruction: On the day of analysis, remove vials from –80 °C, allow them to reach room temperature, and run them in batches of ~10 samples, starting with quality‑control and calibration curves. Use the GC‑MS settings provided in the accompanying document (Agilent 7890A/5975C).
